entries.name: OptimalHypothesisRate.Ref81Lem5
entries.docstring:
This is from [Strong converse exponents for a quantum channel discrimination problem
and quantum-feedback-assisted communication](https://doi.org/10.1007/s00220-016-2645-4), Lemma 5.

It seems like this is actually true for all 0 < α (with appropriate modifications at α = 1), but we only need
it for the case of 1 < α.
entries.snippet:
theorem Ref81Lem5 (ρ σ : MState d) (ε : Prob) (hε : ε < 1) (α : ℝ) (hα : 1 < α) :
    —log β_ ε(ρ‖{σ}) ≤ D̃_ α(ρ‖σ) + —log (1 - ε) *
      (.ofNNReal ⟨α, zero_le_one.trans hα.le⟩) / (.ofNNReal ⟨α - 1, sub_nonneg_of_le hα.le⟩)

entries.name: OptimalHypothesisRate.optimalHypothesisRate_unique
entries.docstring:
On the 1D Hilbert space, the optimal hypothesis testing rate is simply 1 - ε,
since there's nothing to learn. (More generally this would hold whenever ρ=σ.) -
entries.snippet:
theorem optimalHypothesisRate_unique {d : Type*} [Fintype d] [DecidableEq d]
    (ε : Prob) (ρ σ : MState d) [Unique d] : β_ ε(ρ‖{σ}) = 1 - ε

entries.name: ResourceTheory
entries.docstring:
A quantum resource theory extends a `FreeStateTheory` with a collection of free operations. It is
required that any state we can always prepare for free must be free, and this is all then the resource
theory is "minimal", but we can have a more restricted set of operations.
entries.snippet:
class ResourceTheory (ι : Type*) extends FreeStateTheory ι where
  freeOps i j : Set (CPTPMap (H i) (H j))
  nongenerating {i j : ι} {f} (h : f ∈ freeOps i j) : ∀ ρ, IsFree ρ → IsFree (f ρ)
  free_id i : CPTPMap.id ∈ freeOps i i
  free_comp {i j k} (Y : freeOps j k) (X : freeOps i j) : Y.1.compose X.1 ∈ freeOps i k

entries.name: ResourceTheory.maximal
entries.docstring:
Given a `FreeStateTheory`, there is a maximal set of free operations compatible with the free states.
That is the set of all operations that don't generate non-free states from free states. We
call this the maximal resource theory.
entries.snippet: def maximal [FreeStateTheory ι] : ResourceTheory ι where

entries.name: ResourceTheory.IsMaximal
entries.docstring: A resource theory `IsMaximal` if it includes all non-generating operations.
entries.snippet: def IsMaximal (r : ResourceTheory ι) : Prop

entries.name: ResourceTheory.IsTensorial
entries.docstring:
A resource theory `IsTensorial` if it includes tensor products of operations, creating
free states, and discarding. This implies that includes a unit object.
entries.snippet:
structure IsTensorial [UnitalPretheory ι] : Prop where
  prod :  ∀ {i j k l : ι} {f g}, f ∈ freeOps i k → g ∈ freeOps j l → (f ⊗ᶜᵖᵣ g) ∈ freeOps (prod i j) (prod k l)
  create : ∀ {i : ι} (ρ), IsFree ρ → CPTPMap.replacement ρ ∈ freeOps Unital.unit i
  destroy : ∀ (i : ι), CPTPMap.destroy ∈ freeOps i Unital.unit

entries.docstring: The theory `ResourceTheory.maximal` always `IsMaximal`.

entries.name: SteinsLemma.LemmaS2liminf
entries.snippet:
theorem LemmaS2liminf {ε3 : Prob} {ε4 : ℝ≥0} (hε4 : 0 < ε4)
  {d : ℕ → Type*} [∀ n, Fintype (d n)] [∀ n, DecidableEq (d n)] (ρ : (n : ℕ) → MState (d n)) (σ : (n : ℕ) → MState (d n))
  {Rinf : ℝ≥0} (hRinf : Rinf ≥ Filter.atTop.liminf (fun (n : ℕ) ↦ —log β_ ε3(ρ n‖{σ n}) / n))
  :
  (Filter.atTop.liminf (fun (n : ℕ) ↦ ⟪{(ρ n).M ≥ₚ (Real.exp (n * (Rinf + ε4))) • (σ n).M}, (ρ n).M⟫) ≤ 1 - ε3)

  (f : ℕ → ℝ≥0) (hσ : ∀ (i : ℕ), Real.exp (-f i) • (σ₂ i).M ≤ (σ₁ i)) (n : ℕ) :

entries.name: SteinsLemma.LemmaS3_inf
entries.docstring:
Lemma S3 from the paper. What they denote as σₙ and σₙ', we denote as σ₁ and σ₂. The `exp(-o(n))`
we express as a function `f : ℕ → ℝ`, together with the fact that `f` is little-o of `n` (i.e. that
`f =o[.atTop] id`), and then writing `exp(-f)`. We also split LemmaS3 into two parts, the `lim inf` part
and the `lim sup` part. The theorem as written is true for any `f`, but we can restrict to nonnegative
`f` (so, `ℕ → ℝ≥0`) which is easier to work with and more natural in the subsequent proofs.
entries.snippet:
private theorem LemmaS3_inf {ε : Prob}
    {d : ℕ → Type*} [∀ n, Fintype (d n)] [∀ n, DecidableEq (d n)]
    (ρ σ₁ σ₂ : (n : ℕ) → MState (d n))
    (f : ℕ → ℝ≥0) (hf : (f · : ℕ → ℝ) =o[.atTop] (· : ℕ → ℝ))
    (hσ : ∀ i, Real.exp (-f i) • (σ₂ i).M ≤ σ₁ i)
    :
    Filter.atTop.liminf (fun (n : ℕ) ↦ —log β_ ε(ρ n‖{σ₁ n}) / n) ≤
      Filter.atTop.liminf (fun (n : ℕ) ↦ —log β_ ε(ρ n‖{σ₂ n}) / n)

entries.name: SteinsLemma.LemmaS3_sup

private theorem LemmaS3_sup {ε : Prob}
    {d : ℕ → Type*} [∀ n, Fintype (d n)] [∀ n, DecidableEq (d n)]
    (ρ σ₁ σ₂ : (n : ℕ) → MState (d n))
    (f : ℕ → ℝ≥0) (hf : (f · : ℕ → ℝ) =o[.atTop] (· : ℕ → ℝ))

    :
    Filter.atTop.limsup (fun (n : ℕ) ↦ —log β_ ε(ρ n‖{σ₁ n}) / n) ≤
      Filter.atTop.limsup (fun (n : ℕ) ↦ —log β_ ε(ρ n‖{σ₂ n}) / n)

entries.name: SteinsLemma.limit_hypotesting_eq_limit_rel_entropy
entries.docstring:
Theorem 4, which is also called the Generalized quantum Stein's lemma in Hayashi & Yamasaki.
What they state as an equality of limits, which don't exist per se in Mathlib, we state as the existence
of a number (which happens to be `RegularizedRelativeEntResource`) to which both sides converge.
entries.snippet:
theorem limit_hypotesting_eq_limit_rel_entropy (ρ : MState (H i)) (ε : Prob) (hε : 0 < ε ∧ ε < 1) :
    ∃ d : ℝ≥0,
      Filter.atTop.Tendsto (fun n ↦ —log β_ ε(ρ ⊗ᵣ^[n]‖IsFree) / n) (𝓝 d)
      ∧
      Filter.atTop.Tendsto (fun n ↦ (⨅ σ ∈ IsFree, 𝐃(ρ ⊗ᵣ^[n]‖σ)) / n) (𝓝 d)

entries.name: MState.no_cloning
entries.docstring:
The **No-cloning theorem**, saying that if states `ψ` and `φ` can both be perfectly cloned using a
unitary `U` and a fiducial state `f`, and they aren't identical (their inner product is less than 1),
then the two states must be orthogonal to begin with. In short: only orthogonal states can be simultaneously
cloned.
entries.snippet:
theorem no_cloning {U : 𝐔[d × d]}
  (hψ : U ◃ pure (ψ ⊗ᵠ f) = pure (ψ ⊗ᵠ ψ))
  (hφ : U ◃ pure (φ ⊗ᵠ f) = pure (φ ⊗ᵠ φ))
  (H : ⟪pure ψ, pure φ⟫_Prob < (1 : ℝ)) :
    ⟪pure ψ, pure φ⟫_Prob = (0 : ℝ)

entries.name: HermitianMat.conj
entries.docstring:
The Hermitian matrix given by conjugating by a (possibly rectangular) Matrix. If we required `B` to be
square, this would apply to any `Semigroup`+`StarMul` (as proved by `IsSelfAdjoint.conjugate`). But this lets
us conjugate to other sizes too, as is done in e.g. Kraus operators. That is, it's a _heterogeneous_ conjguation.

entries.name: HermitianMat.mat_cfc_mul
entries.docstring:
We don't have a direct analog of `cfc_mul`, since we can't generally multiply
to HermitianMat's to get another one, so the theorem statement wouldn't be well-typed.
But, we can say that the matrices are always equal. See `cfc_conj` for the coe-free
analog to multiplication.
entries.snippet: theorem mat_cfc_mul : (A.cfc (f * g)).mat = A.cfc f * A.cfc g

entries.name: HermitianMat.mat_cfc_mul_apply
entries.snippet: theorem mat_cfc_mul_apply : (A.cfc (fun x ↦ f x * g x)).mat = A.cfc f * A.cfc g

entries.name: HermitianMat.cfc_comp_apply

entries.name: HermitianMat.cfc_conj

    {f : X → ℝ → ℝ} {S : Set X} {T : Set ℝ}

    {x₀ : X} (hx₀ : x₀ ∈ S) {ε : ℝ} (hε : 0 < ε) :
    ∃ U ∈ nhds x₀, ∀ x ∈ U ∩ S, ∀ t ∈ T, ‖f x t - f x₀ t‖ < ε

entries.name: Commute.exists_HermitianMat_cfc

If two matrices A and B commute, then they is a common matrix with which they are both CFCs of.
This is a variant of the common theorem that "commuting matrices can be simultaneously diagonalized."

entries.name: HermitianMat.log
entries.docstring:
Matrix logarithm (base e) of a Hermitian matrix, as given by the elementwise
  real logarithm of the diagonal in a diagonalized form, using `Real.log`

  Note that this means that the nullspace of the image includes all of the nullspace of the
  original matrix. This contrasts to the standard definition, which is typically defined for
  positive *definite* matrices, and the nullspace of the image is exactly the
  (λ=1)-eigenspace of the original matrix. (We also get the (λ=-1)-eigenspace here!)

  It coincides with a standard definition if A is positive definite.

such that `P^2 = P` and `P * A * P ≤ P * B * P` in the Loewner order.

entries.name: HermitianMat.projLT
entries.docstring:
Projector onto the positive eigenspace of `B - A`. Accessible by the notation
`{A <ₚ B}`, which is scoped to `HermitianMat`. Compare with `proj_le`.
entries.snippet: noncomputable def projLT (A B : HermitianMat n 𝕜) : HermitianMat n 𝕜

entries.name: HermitianMat.projLE_def
entries.snippet: theorem projLE_def : {A ≤ₚ B} = (B - A).cfc (fun x ↦ if 0 ≤ x then 1 else 0)

entries.name: HermitianMat.projLT_def
entries.snippet: theorem projLT_def : {A <ₚ B} = (B - A).cfc (fun x ↦ if 0 < x then 1 else 0)

entries.name: HermitianMat.projLE_sq
entries.snippet: theorem projLE_sq : {A ≤ₚ B}^2 = {A ≤ₚ B}

entries.name: HermitianMat.projLT_sq
entries.snippet: theorem projLT_sq : {A <ₚ B}^2 = {A <ₚ B}

entries.name: HermitianMat.projLE_zero_cfc
entries.snippet: theorem projLE_zero_cfc : {0 ≤ₚ A} = A.cfc (fun x ↦ if 0 ≤ x then 1 else 0)

entries.name: HermitianMat.projLT_zero_cfc
entries.snippet: theorem projLT_zero_cfc : {0 <ₚ A} = A.cfc (fun x ↦ if 0 < x then 1 else 0)

entries.snippet: theorem projLE_zero_cfc' : {A ≤ₚ 0} = A.cfc (fun x ↦ if x ≤ 0 then 1 else 0)

entries.name: HermitianMat.projLT_zero_cfc'
entries.snippet: theorem projLT_zero_cfc' : {A <ₚ 0} = A.cfc (fun x ↦ if x < 0 then 1 else 0)

entries.snippet: theorem projLE_nonneg : 0 ≤ {A ≤ₚ B}

entries.name: HermitianMat.projLT_nonneg

entries.name: HermitianMat.projLE_le_one
entries.snippet: theorem projLE_le_one : {A ≤ₚ B} ≤ 1

entries.name: HermitianMat.projLE_mul_nonneg
entries.snippet: theorem projLE_mul_nonneg : 0 ≤ {A ≤ₚ B}.mat * (B - A).mat

entries.name: HermitianMat.projLE_mul_le
entries.snippet: theorem projLE_mul_le : {A ≤ₚ B}.mat * A.mat ≤ {A ≤ₚ B}.mat * B.mat

entries.name: HermitianMat.proj_le_add_lt

@[simp]
theorem proj_le_add_lt : {A <ₚ B} + {B ≤ₚ A} = 1

entries.snippet: theorem conj_lt_add_conj_le : A.conj {A <ₚ 0} + A.conj {0 ≤ₚ A} = A

theorem supportProj_eq_proj_lt_add_proj_lt (A : HermitianMat n 𝕜) :

entries.name: HermitianMat.nonneg_iff_inner_nonneg
entries.docstring:
The self-duality of the PSD cone: a matrix is PSD iff its inner product with all
nonnegative matrices is non-negative.
entries.snippet:
theorem nonneg_iff_inner_nonneg (A : HermitianMat n 𝕜) :
    0 ≤ A ↔ ∀ B, 0 ≤ B → 0 ≤ ⟪A, B⟫

theorem reindex_refl (A : HermitianMat d 𝕜) :

entries.name: HermitianMat.reindex_reindex

entries.name: HermitianMat.reindex_one
entries.snippet:

theorem reindex_one [DecidableEq d] [DecidableEq d₂] :

entries.name: HermitianMat.reindex_add
entries.snippet:
@[simp]
theorem reindex_add : A.reindex e + B.reindex e = (A + B).reindex e

entries.name: HermitianMat.reindex_sub
entries.snippet:
@[simp]
theorem reindex_sub  : A.reindex e - B.reindex e = (A - B).reindex e

entries.name: HermitianMat.reindex_neg

entries.name: HermitianMat.reindex_smul

entries.name: HermitianMat.reindex_conj
entries.snippet:
@[simp]
theorem reindex_conj [Fintype d₂] [Fintype d] (B : Matrix d₃ d₂ 𝕜) :

entries.name: HermitianMat.conj_submatrix
entries.snippet:
theorem conj_submatrix (B : Matrix d₂ d₄ 𝕜) (e : d₃ ≃ d₂) (f : d → d₄) :

entries.name: HermitianMat.reindex_eq_conj
entries.snippet: theorem reindex_eq_conj [DecidableEq d] (e : d ≃ d₂) : A.reindex e = A.conj (Matrix.reindex e (.refl d) 1)

entries.name: HermitianMat.ker_reindex
entries.snippet:
theorem ker_reindex :
    (A.reindex e).ker = A.ker.comap (LinearEquiv.euclidean_of_relabel 𝕜 e).toLinearMap

entries.name: HermitianMat.ker_reindex_le_iff
entries.snippet:
@[simp]
theorem ker_reindex_le_iff :
    (A.reindex e).ker ≤ (B.reindex e).ker ↔ A.ker ≤ B.ker

entries.name: HermitianMat.rpow
entries.docstring:
Matrix power of a positive semidefinite matrix, as given by the elementwise
  real power of the diagonal in a diagonalized form.

  Note that this has the usual `Real.rpow` caveats, such as 0 to the power -1 giving 0.
entries.snippet: def rpow (A : HermitianMat d 𝕜) (r : ℝ) : HermitianMat d 𝕜

entries.name: HermitianMat.instRPow
entries.snippet: instance instRPow : Pow (HermitianMat d 𝕜) ℝ

entries.snippet:
theorem rpow_conj_unitary (A : HermitianMat d 𝕜) (U : Matrix.unitaryGroup d 𝕜) (r : ℝ) :
    (HermitianMat.conj U.val A) ^ r = HermitianMat.conj U.val (A ^ r)

entries.name: HermitianMat.pow_eq_rpow
entries.snippet: theorem pow_eq_rpow : A ^ r = A.rpow r

entries.name: HermitianMat.rpow_eq_cfc

entries.name: HermitianMat.rpow_kron_diagonal

private lemma rpow_kron_diagonal
    (a : d → ℝ) (b : d₂ → ℝ) (r : ℝ) (ha : ∀ i, 0 ≤ a i) (hb : ∀ j, 0 ≤ b j) :
    ((diagonal ℂ a) ⊗ₖ (diagonal ℂ b)) ^ r =
    ((diagonal ℂ a) ^ r) ⊗ₖ ((diagonal ℂ b) ^ r)

    conj (A ⊗ₖ B) (C ⊗ₖ D) = conj A C ⊗ₖ conj B D

entries.snippet:
lemma rpow_kron
    {A : HermitianMat d ℂ} {B : HermitianMat d₂ ℂ} (r : ℝ) (hA : 0 ≤ A) (hB : 0 ≤ B) :

entries.name: HermitianMat.continuousOn_rpow_joint_nonneg_pos

@[fun_prop]
theorem continuousOn_rpow_joint_nonneg_pos

entries.name: HermitianMat.cfc_sq_rpow_eq_cfc_rpow

theorem cfc_sq_rpow_eq_cfc_rpow
    (A : HermitianMat d ℂ) (hA : 0 ≤ A) (p : ℝ) (hp : 0 < p) :
    (A ^ 2).cfc (fun x => x ^ (p/2)) = A.cfc (fun x => x ^ p)

entries.name: HermitianMat.trace_rpow_eq_sum
entries.docstring: Tr[A^p] = ∑ᵢ λᵢ^p for a Hermitian matrix A.
entries.snippet:
lemma trace_rpow_eq_sum (A : HermitianMat d ℂ) (p : ℝ) :
    (A ^ p).trace = ∑ i, (A.H.eigenvalues i) ^ p

entries.name: HermitianMat.rpowApprox
entries.docstring:
Finite integral approximation for the rpow monotonicity proof.
    Same integrand as `logApprox` but with weight `t ^ q`.
entries.snippet: noncomputable def rpowApprox (A : HermitianMat d ℂ) (q T : ℝ) : HermitianMat d ℂ

entries.name: HermitianMat.rpowApprox_mono
entries.snippet:
theorem rpowApprox_mono {A B : HermitianMat d ℂ} (hA : A.mat.PosDef) (hB : B.mat.PosDef)
    (hAB : A ≤ B) (hq : 0 ≤ q) (T : ℝ) (hT : 0 < T) :
    rpowApprox A q T ≤ rpowApprox B q T

entries.name: HermitianMat.scalarRpowApprox
entries.docstring: The scalar function underlying rpowApprox via the CFC.
entries.snippet: noncomputable def scalarRpowApprox (q T x : ℝ) : ℝ

entries.name: HermitianMat.rpowApprox_eq_cfc_scalar
entries.snippet:
theorem rpowApprox_eq_cfc_scalar (A : HermitianMat d ℂ) (hA : A.mat.PosDef) (q T : ℝ)
    (hq : 0 ≤ q) (hT : 0 < T) :
    rpowApprox A q T = A.cfc (scalarRpowApprox q T)

entries.name: HermitianMat.rpowConst
entries.docstring:
The positive constant arising from the resolvent integral.
    Equal to `∫ u in Set.Ioi 0, u ^ (q-1) / (1+u)` = `π / sin(π q)`,
    but we only need its positivity.
entries.snippet: noncomputable def rpowConst (q : ℝ) : ℝ

entries.name: HermitianMat.rpowConst_integrableOn
entries.docstring: The integrand `u ^ (q-1) / (1+u)` is integrable on `(0, ∞)` for `0 < q < 1`.
entries.snippet:
lemma rpowConst_integrableOn (hq : 0 < q) (hq1 : q < 1) :
    IntegrableOn (fun u : ℝ => u ^ (q - 1) / (1 + u)) (Set.Ioi 0)

entries.name: HermitianMat.rpowConst_pos
entries.snippet: lemma rpowConst_pos (hq : 0 < q) (hq1 : q < 1) : 0 < rpowConst q

entries.name: HermitianMat.scalarRpowApprox_tendsto
entries.docstring:
The scalar rpow approximation converges pointwise.
    `scalarRpowApprox q T x → rpowConst q * (x^q - 1)` as `T → ∞`.
entries.snippet:
lemma scalarRpowApprox_tendsto {x : ℝ} (hx : 0 < x) (hq : 0 < q) (hq1 : q < 1) :
    Filter.Tendsto (fun T => scalarRpowApprox q T x) atTop (nhds (rpowConst q * (x ^ q - 1)))

entries.name: HermitianMat.tendsto_rpowApprox
entries.docstring: The matrix rpow approximation converges: `rpowApprox A q T → rpowConst q • (A^q - 1)`.
entries.snippet:
lemma tendsto_rpowApprox (hA : A.mat.PosDef) (hq : 0 < q) (hq1 : q < 1) :
    Tendsto (rpowApprox A q) atTop (nhds (rpowConst q • (A ^ q - 1)))

entries.name: HermitianMat.rpow_le_rpow_of_posDef
entries.snippet:
theorem rpow_le_rpow_of_posDef (hA : A.mat.PosDef) (hAB : A ≤ B)
    (hq : 0 < q) (hq1 : q ≤ 1) : A ^ q ≤ B ^ q

entries.name: HermitianMat.rpow_le_rpow_of_le
entries.docstring:
The **Löwner—Heinz theorem**: for matrices A and B, if `0 ≤ A ≤ B` and `0 < q ≤ 1`,
then `A^q ≤ B^q`. That is, real roots are operator monotone.
entries.snippet:
theorem rpow_le_rpow_of_le (hA : 0 ≤ A) (hAB : A ≤ B)
    (hq : 0 < q) (hq1 : q ≤ 1) : A ^ q ≤ B ^ q

entries.name: HermitianMat.lieb_thirring_le_one
entries.docstring:
An inequality of Lieb-Thirring type. For 0 < r ≤ 1:
  `Tr[B^r A^r B^r] ≤ Tr[(B A B)^r]`.
entries.snippet:
lemma lieb_thirring_le_one
    {A B : HermitianMat d ℂ} (hA : 0 ≤ A) (hB : 0 ≤ B)
    {r : ℝ} (hq0 : 0 < r) (hq1 : q ≤ r) :
    ((A ^ r).conj (B ^ r).mat).trace ≤ ((A.conj B.mat) ^ r).trace

entries.name: HermitianMat.trace_rpow_add_le
entries.snippet:
lemma trace_rpow_add_le
    {A B : HermitianMat d ℂ} (hA : 0 ≤ A) (hB : 0 ≤ B)
    (p : ℝ) (hp : 0 < p) (hp1 : p ≤ 1) :
    ((A + B) ^ p).trace ≤ (A ^ p).trace + (B ^ p).trace

entries.name: schattenNorm
entries.docstring: The Schatten p-norm of a matrix A is (Tr[(A*A)^(p/2)])^(1/p).
entries.snippet: noncomputable def schattenNorm (A : Matrix d d ℂ) (p : ℝ) : ℝ

entries.name: schattenNorm_hermitian_pow
entries.snippet:
theorem schattenNorm_hermitian_pow {A : HermitianMat d ℂ} (hA : 0 ≤ A) {p : ℝ} (hp : 0 < p) :
    schattenNorm A.mat p = (A ^ p).trace ^ (1/p)

entries.name: schattenNorm_nonneg
entries.snippet:
lemma schattenNorm_nonneg (A : Matrix d d ℂ) (p : ℝ) :
    0 ≤ schattenNorm A p

entries.name: schattenNorm_pow_eq
entries.snippet:
lemma schattenNorm_pow_eq
  (A : HermitianMat d ℂ) (hA : 0 ≤ A) (p k : ℝ) (hp : 0 < p) (hk : 0 < k) :
    schattenNorm (A ^ k).mat p = (schattenNorm A.mat (k * p)) ^ k

entries.name: trace_eq_schattenNorm_rpow
entries.snippet:
lemma trace_eq_schattenNorm_rpow
    (A : HermitianMat d ℂ) (hA : 0 ≤ A) (r : ℝ) (hr : 0 < r) :
    (A ^ r).trace = (schattenNorm A.mat r) ^ r

entries.name: schattenNorm_trace_as_eigenvalue_sum
entries.snippet:
lemma schattenNorm_trace_as_eigenvalue_sum (A : Matrix d d ℂ) (p : ℝ) :
    RCLike.re ((Matrix.isHermitian_mul_conjTranspose_self A.conjTranspose).cfc (· ^ (p/2))).trace =
    ∑ i : d, ((Matrix.isHermitian_mul_conjTranspose_self A.conjTranspose).eigenvalues i) ^ (p/2)

entries.name: schattenNorm_rpow_eq_sum_singularValues
entries.snippet:
lemma schattenNorm_rpow_eq_sum_singularValues (A : Matrix d d ℂ) {p : ℝ} (hp : 0 < p) :
    schattenNorm A p ^ p = ∑ i : d, singularValues A i ^ p

entries.name: schattenNorm_eq_sum_singularValues_rpow
entries.snippet:
lemma schattenNorm_eq_sum_singularValues_rpow (A : Matrix d d ℂ) {p : ℝ} (hp : 0 < p) :
    schattenNorm A p = (∑ i : d, singularValues A i ^ p) ^ (1/p)

entries.name: schattenNorm_rpow_eq_sum_sorted
entries.docstring: `‖A‖_p^p` equals the same sum over sorted singular values.
entries.snippet:
lemma schattenNorm_rpow_eq_sum_sorted (A : Matrix d d ℂ) {p : ℝ} (hp : 0 < p) :
    schattenNorm A p ^ p =
    ∑ i : Fin (Fintype.card d), singularValuesSorted A i ^ p

entries.name: HermitianMat.trace_young
entries.docstring:
Scalar trace Young inequality for PSD matrices:
⟪A, B⟫ ≤ Tr[A^p]/p + Tr[B^q]/q for PSD A, B and conjugate p, q > 1.
entries.snippet:
lemma HermitianMat.trace_young
    (A B : HermitianMat d ℂ) (hA : 0 ≤ A) (hB : 0 ≤ B)
    (p q : ℝ) (hp : 1 < p) (hpq : 1/p + 1/q = 1) :
    ⟪A, B⟫_ℝ ≤ (A ^ p).trace / p + (B ^ q).trace / q

entries.name: conjTranspose_half_mul_eq_conj
entries.docstring:
For PSD `A` and Hermitian `B`, the product
`C = A^{1/2} * B` satisfies `C^* C = (A.conj B.mat).mat = B * A * B`.
entries.snippet:
lemma conjTranspose_half_mul_eq_conj
    {A B : HermitianMat d ℂ} (hA : 0 ≤ A) :
    ((A ^ (1/2 : ℝ)).mat * B.mat).conjTranspose * ((A ^ (1/2 : ℝ)).mat * B.mat)
    = (A.conj B.mat).mat

entries.name: schattenNorm_half_mul_rpow_eq_trace_conj
entries.snippet:
lemma schattenNorm_half_mul_rpow_eq_trace_conj
    {A B : HermitianMat d ℂ} (hA : 0 ≤ A)
    {α : ℝ} (hα : 0 < α) :
    (schattenNorm ((A ^ (1/2 : ℝ)).mat * B.mat) (2 * α)) ^ (2 * α) =
    ((A.conj B.mat) ^ α).trace

entries.name: schattenNorm_mul_le
HermitianMat.trace_rpow_conj_le
entries.snippet:
lemma HermitianMat.trace_rpow_conj_le
    {A B : HermitianMat d ℂ} (hA : 0 ≤ A) (hB : 0 ≤ B)
    {α p q : ℝ} (hα : 0 < α) (hp : 0 < p) (hq : 0 < q)
    (hpq : 1 / (2 * α) = 1 / p + 1 / q) :
    ((A.conj B.mat) ^ α).trace ≤
    (((A ^ (p / 2)).trace) ^ (1 / p) * ((B ^ q).trace) ^ (1 / q)) ^ (2 * α)

entries.name: HermitianMat.trace
entries.docstring:
The trace of the matrix. This requires a `IsMaximalSelfAdjoint R α` instance, and then maps from
  `HermitianMat n α` to `R`. This means that the trace of (say) a `HermitianMat n ℤ` gives values in ℤ,
  but that the trace of a `HermitianMat n ℂ` gives values in ℝ. The fact that traces are "automatically"
  real reduces coercions down the line.
entries.snippet: def trace (A : HermitianMat n α) : R

entries.name: HermitianMat.trace_eq_trace

entries.snippet: theorem trace_eq_trace (A : HermitianMat n α) : algebraMap R α A.trace = Matrix.trace A.mat

entries.name: Matrix.Isometry
entries.docstring:
An isometry is a matrix `A` such that `AAᴴ = 1`. Compare with a unitary, which
requires `AAᴴ = AᴴA = 1`. It is common to claim that, in a finite-dimensional vector
space, a two-sided isometry (`A.Isometry ∧ Aᴴ.Isometry`) must be square and therefore unitary;
this is does not work out so well here, since a `Matrix m n R` can be a two-sided isometry,
but cannot be a `unitary` since the rows and columns are index by different labels.
entries.snippet: def Matrix.Isometry (A : Matrix d d₂ R) : Prop

entries.name: Matrix.IsHermitian.cfc_eq_any_isometry
entries.docstring:
Generalizes `Matrix.IsHermitian.cfc.eq_1`, which gives a definition for the matrix CFC in terms of
`Matrix.IsHermitian.eigenvalues` and `Matrix.IsHermitian.eigenvectorUnitary`, to show that the CFC works
similarly for _any_ diagonalization by a two-sided isometry.

entries.name: Matrix.IsHermitian.cfc_eq_any_unitary
entries.docstring:
Generalizes `Matrix.IsHermitian.cfc.eq_1`, which gives a definition for the matrix CFC in terms of
`Matrix.IsHermitian.eigenvalues` and `Matrix.IsHermitian.eigenvectorUnitary`, to show that the CFC works
similarly for _any_ diagonalization.
entries.snippet:
theorem Matrix.IsHermitian.cfc_eq_any_unitary {n 𝕜 : Type*} [RCLike 𝕜] [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n]
  {A : Matrix n n 𝕜} (hA : A.IsHermitian) {U : unitaryGroup n 𝕜} {D : n → ℝ}
  (hUD : A = U.val * diagonal (RCLike.ofReal ∘ D) * star U.val) (f : ℝ → ℝ) :
    hA.cfc f = U.val * diagonal (RCLike.ofReal ∘ f ∘ D) * star U.val

entries.name: Matrix.IsDiag.exists_cfc
entries.docstring:
If a matrix is diagonalized by a unitary matrix, then it can be written as a
CFC of a (particular, canonical) diagonal matrix.
entries.snippet:
theorem Matrix.IsDiag.exists_cfc {U : Matrix.unitaryGroup d 𝕜} {M : Matrix d d 𝕜}
  (hU : (U.val * M * Uᴴ).IsDiag) (hM : M.IsHermitian) (e : d ≃ Fin (Fintype.card d)) :
       ∃ f : ℝ → ℝ,
    M = cfc f (Uᴴ * (Matrix.diagonal fun x => ↑↑(e x)) * U.val)

entries.name: singularValues
entries.docstring:
The singular values of a square complex matrix `A`, defined as the square
roots of the eigenvalues of `A†A`. These are indexed by `d` without a
particular ordering.

Note: We use `A.conjTranspose` as the argument to `isHermitian_mul_conjTranspose_self`
so that the underlying Hermitian matrix is `A† * A` (matching the convention in `schattenNorm`).
entries.snippet: def singularValues (A : Matrix d d ℂ) : d → ℝ

entries.name: singularValues_nonneg
entries.docstring: Singular values are nonneg.
entries.snippet:
lemma singularValues_nonneg (A : Matrix d d ℂ) (i : d) :
    0 ≤ singularValues A i

entries.name: singularValuesSorted
entries.docstring:
The sorted singular values of a square complex matrix, in decreasing order,
indexed by `Fin (Fintype.card d)`.

We define them by sorting the multiset of singular values.
entries.snippet:
noncomputable def singularValuesSorted (A : Matrix d d ℂ) :
    Fin (Fintype.card d) → ℝ

entries.name: singularValuesSorted_nonneg
entries.docstring: Sorted singular values are nonneg.
entries.snippet:
lemma singularValuesSorted_nonneg (A : Matrix d d ℂ) (i : Fin (Fintype.card d)) :
    0 ≤ singularValuesSorted A i

entries.name: sum_singularValues_rpow_eq_sum_sorted
entries.docstring: The sum `∑ singularValues A i ^ p` equals the sum over sorted singular values.
entries.snippet:
lemma sum_singularValues_rpow_eq_sum_sorted (A : Matrix d d ℂ) (p : ℝ) :
    ∑ i : d, singularValues A i ^ p =
    ∑ i : Fin (Fintype.card d), singularValuesSorted A i ^ p

entries.name: singularValuesSorted_antitone
entries.docstring: Sorted singular values are antitone (decreasing).
entries.snippet:
lemma singularValuesSorted_antitone (A : Matrix d d ℂ) :
    Antitone (singularValuesSorted A)

entries.docstring: The product of nonneg antitone sequences is antitone.

lemma antitone_mul_of_antitone_nonneg {n : ℕ}

entries.docstring: The `k`-th compound (exterior-power) matrix of `M`.
entries.snippet:
noncomputable def compoundMatrix (M : Matrix d d ℂ) (k : ℕ) :
    Matrix {S : Finset d // S.card = k} {S : Finset d // S.card = k} ℂ

entries.name: cauchyBinet
entries.docstring:
**Cauchy–Binet formula** for rectangular matrices: if `A` is `m × n` and `B` is
`n × m`, then `det(A * B) = ∑_S det(A[:,S]) * det(B[S,:])` where the sum is
over `m`-element subsets `S` of the column/row index.
entries.snippet:
lemma cauchyBinet {m : ℕ} {n : Type*} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] [LinearOrder n]
    {R : Type*} [CommRing R]
    (A : Matrix (Fin m) n R) (B : Matrix n (Fin m) R) :
    (A * B).det = ∑ S : {S : Finset n // S.card = m},
      (A.submatrix id (S.1.orderEmbOfFin S.2)).det *
      (B.submatrix (S.1.orderEmbOfFin S.2) id).det

entries.name: compoundMatrix_mul
entries.docstring: The `compoundMatrix` of a product is the product of the `compoundMatrix`s.
entries.snippet:
lemma compoundMatrix_mul (M N : Matrix d d ℂ) (k : ℕ) :
    compoundMatrix (M * N) k = compoundMatrix M k * compoundMatrix N k

entries.name: compoundMatrix_conjTranspose
entries.docstring: `compoundMatrix` commutes with `conjTranspose`.
entries.snippet:
lemma compoundMatrix_conjTranspose (M : Matrix d d ℂ) (k : ℕ) :
    compoundMatrix M.conjTranspose k = (compoundMatrix M k).conjTranspose

entries.name: compoundMatrix_diagonal
entries.docstring:
The compound matrix of a diagonal matrix is diagonal, with entries being
products of eigenvalues over k-subsets.
entries.snippet:
lemma compoundMatrix_diagonal (f : d → ℂ) (k : ℕ) :
    compoundMatrix (Matrix.diagonal f) k =
    Matrix.diagonal (fun S : {S : Finset d // S.card = k} =>
      ∏ i : Fin k, f (S.1.orderEmbOfFin S.2 i))

entries.name: singularValues_compoundMatrix_eq
entries.docstring:
The eigenvalues of the compound matrix of a Hermitian matrix are the products
of eigenvalues over k-subsets. More precisely, the singular values of
`compoundMatrix M k` are the square roots of products of eigenvalues of M†M
over k-subsets.
entries.snippet:
lemma singularValues_compoundMatrix_eq (M : Matrix d d ℂ) (k : ℕ) :
    ∀ (S : {S : Finset d // S.card = k}),
    ∃ (j : {S : Finset d // S.card = k}),
    singularValues (compoundMatrix M k) j =
    ∏ i : Fin k, singularValues M (S.1.orderEmbOfFin S.2 i)

entries.name: prod_le_prod_sorted
entries.docstring:
The product of nonneg values over a k-subset is at most the product of the
    k largest values.
entries.snippet:
lemma prod_le_prod_sorted {n : ℕ} {f : Fin n → ℝ}
    (hf : Antitone f) (hf_nn : ∀ i, 0 ≤ f i)
    (k : ℕ) (hk : k ≤ n)
    (g : Fin k → Fin n) (hg : Function.Injective g) :
    ∏ i : Fin k, f (g i) ≤ ∏ i : Fin k, f ⟨i.val, by omega⟩

entries.name: singularValuesSorted_zero_eq_sup
entries.docstring: The 0th sorted singular value is the maximum of the singular values.
entries.snippet:
lemma singularValuesSorted_zero_eq_sup {e : Type*} [Fintype e] [DecidableEq e]
    (A : Matrix e e ℂ) (h : 0 < Fintype.card e) :
    singularValuesSorted A ⟨0, h⟩ = Finset.sup' Finset.univ
      (Finset.univ_nonempty_iff.mpr (Fintype.card_pos_iff.mp h))
      (singularValues A)

entries.name: singularValues_mem_sorted
entries.docstring: Each singular value appears in the sorted list.
entries.snippet:
lemma singularValues_mem_sorted {e : Type*} [Fintype e] [DecidableEq e]
    (A : Matrix e e ℂ) (i : e) :
    ∃ j : Fin (Fintype.card e), singularValues A i = singularValuesSorted A j

entries.name: singularValuesSorted_mem_values
entries.docstring: Each sorted singular value appears among the original singular values.
entries.snippet:
lemma singularValuesSorted_mem_values {e : Type*} [Fintype e] [DecidableEq e]
    (A : Matrix e e ℂ) (j : Fin (Fintype.card e)) :
    ∃ i : e, singularValuesSorted A j = singularValues A i

entries.name: singularValues_compoundMatrix_perm
entries.docstring: Stronger version of `singularValues_compoundMatrix_eq` that exposes the permutation.
entries.snippet:
lemma singularValues_compoundMatrix_perm (M : Matrix d d ℂ) (k : ℕ) :
    ∃ σ : {S : Finset d // S.card = k} ≃ {S : Finset d // S.card = k},
    ∀ S, singularValues (compoundMatrix M k) (σ S) =
    ∏ i : Fin k, singularValues M (S.1.orderEmbOfFin S.2 i)

entries.name: singularValues_compoundMatrix_rev
entries.docstring:
Converse of `singularValues_compoundMatrix_eq`: every singular value of the
    compound matrix is a product of singular values of M over some k-subset.
entries.snippet:
lemma singularValues_compoundMatrix_rev (M : Matrix d d ℂ) (k : ℕ)
    (j : {S : Finset d // S.card = k}) :
    ∃ (S : {S : Finset d // S.card = k}),
    singularValues (compoundMatrix M k) j =
    ∏ i : Fin k, singularValues M (S.1.orderEmbOfFin S.2 i)

entries.name: exists_sorting_equiv
entries.docstring:
There exists a bijection `σ : Fin (card d) ≃ d` such that
    `singularValues M (σ i) = singularValuesSorted M i` for all `i`.
entries.snippet:
lemma exists_sorting_equiv (M : Matrix d d ℂ) :
    ∃ σ : Fin (Fintype.card d) ≃ d,
    ∀ i, singularValues M (σ i) = singularValuesSorted M i

entries.name: prod_singularValues_subset_le_sorted_prod
entries.docstring:
For any k-subset S of d, the product of singular values over S is ≤ the
    product of the top k sorted singular values.
entries.snippet:
lemma prod_singularValues_subset_le_sorted_prod (M : Matrix d d ℂ) (k : ℕ)
    (hk : k ≤ Fintype.card d) (S : {S : Finset d // S.card = k}) :
    ∏ i : Fin k, singularValues M (S.1.orderEmbOfFin S.2 i) ≤
    ∏ i : Fin k, singularValuesSorted M ⟨i.val, by omega⟩

entries.name: exists_subset_prod_eq_sorted_prod
entries.snippet:
lemma exists_subset_prod_eq_sorted_prod (M : Matrix d d ℂ) (k : ℕ)
    (hk : k ≤ Fintype.card d) :
    ∃ S : {S : Finset d // S.card = k},
    ∏ i : Fin k, singularValues M (S.1.orderEmbOfFin S.2 i) =
    ∏ i : Fin k, singularValuesSorted M ⟨i.val, by omega⟩

entries.name: prod_singularValuesSorted_eq_compoundSV
entries.snippet:
lemma prod_singularValuesSorted_eq_compoundSV (M : Matrix d d ℂ) (k : ℕ)
    (hk : k ≤ Fintype.card d) :
    ∏ i : Fin k, singularValuesSorted M ⟨i.val, by omega⟩ =
    singularValuesSorted (compoundMatrix M k) ⟨0, by
      have : Fintype.card {S : Finset d // S.card = k} = (Fintype.card d).choose k := by
        simp [Fintype.card_subtype]
      rw [this]; exact Nat.choose_pos hk⟩

entries.name: IsHermitian.inner_le_sup_eigenvalue_mul_inner
entries.docstring:
The **Rayleigh quotient bound**:
For a Hermitian matrix H with eigenvalues λ, we have
`v† H v ≤ (max λ) · v† v` for all v.
entries.snippet:
lemma IsHermitian.inner_le_sup_eigenvalue_mul_inner
    {e : Type*} [Fintype e] [DecidableEq e]
    (H : Matrix e e ℂ) (hH : H.IsHermitian)
    (he : 0 < Fintype.card e)
    (v : e → ℂ) :
    Complex.re (star v ⬝ᵥ H.mulVec v) ≤
    Finset.sup' Finset.univ
      (Finset.univ_nonempty_iff.mpr (Fintype.card_pos_iff.mp he))
      hH.eigenvalues * Complex.re (star v ⬝ᵥ v)

entries.name: eigenvalue_le_singularValuesSorted_sq
entries.snippet:
lemma eigenvalue_le_singularValuesSorted_sq {e : Type*} [Fintype e] [DecidableEq e]
    (A : Matrix e e ℂ) (h : 0 < Fintype.card e) (i : e) :
  (isHermitian_mul_conjTranspose_self A.conjTranspose).eigenvalues i ≤
    (singularValuesSorted A ⟨0, h⟩) ^ 2

entries.name: quadratic_form_le_singularValuesSorted_sq
entries.docstring: The quadratic form of `A† A` is bounded by (max singular value)² * ‖v‖².
entries.snippet:
lemma quadratic_form_le_singularValuesSorted_sq {e : Type*} [Fintype e] [DecidableEq e]
    (A : Matrix e e ℂ) (h : 0 < Fintype.card e) (v : e → ℂ) :
  Complex.re (star v ⬝ᵥ (A.conjTranspose * A).mulVec v) ≤
    (singularValuesSorted A ⟨0, h⟩) ^ 2 * Complex.re (star v ⬝ᵥ v)

entries.name: singularValuesSorted_mul_le
entries.docstring:
The largest singular value of a matrix product is at most the product of the
largest singular values: `σ₁(M * N) ≤ σ₁(M) * σ₁(N)`.
This is operator-norm submultiplicativity.
entries.snippet:
lemma singularValuesSorted_mul_le {e : Type*} [Fintype e] [DecidableEq e]
    (M N : Matrix e e ℂ) (h : 0 < Fintype.card e) :
    singularValuesSorted (M * N) ⟨0, h⟩ ≤
    singularValuesSorted M ⟨0, h⟩ * singularValuesSorted N ⟨0, h⟩

entries.name: horn_weak_log_majorization
entries.docstring:
Horn's inequality (weak log-majorization of singular values):
For all `k`, `∏_{i<k} σ↓ᵢ(AB) ≤ ∏_{i<k} σ↓ᵢ(A) · σ↓ᵢ(B)`.
This follows from submultiplicativity of the operator norm applied to
exterior powers of the matrices.
entries.snippet:
lemma horn_weak_log_majorization (A B : Matrix d d ℂ) (k : ℕ)
    (hk : k ≤ Fintype.card d) :
    ∏ i : Fin k, singularValuesSorted (A * B) ⟨i.val, by omega⟩ ≤
    ∏ i : Fin k, (singularValuesSorted A ⟨i.val, by omega⟩ *
                   singularValuesSorted B ⟨i.val, by omega⟩)

entries.docstring: Weak log-majorization is preserved under positive powers.

lemma rpow_preserves_weak_log_maj {n : ℕ}
    {x y : Fin n → ℝ}
    (hx_nn : ∀ i, 0 ≤ x i) (hy_nn : ∀ i, 0 ≤ y i)
    (h_log_maj : ∀ (k : ℕ) (_ : k ≤ n),
      ∏ i : Fin k, x ⟨i.val, by omega⟩ ≤
      ∏ i : Fin k, y ⟨i.val, by omega⟩)
    {r : ℝ} (hr : 0 < r) :
    ∀ (k : ℕ) (_ : k ≤ n),
      ∏ i : Fin k, (fun j => x j ^ r) ⟨i.val, by omega⟩ ≤
      ∏ i : Fin k, (fun j => y j ^ r) ⟨i.val, by omega⟩

    ∑ i : Fin (Fintype.card d), singularValuesSorted (A * B) i ^ r ≤
    ∑ i : Fin (Fintype.card d),
      (singularValuesSorted A i ^ r * singularValuesSorted B i ^ r)

entries.name: holder_step_for_singularValues
entries.docstring:
The finite-sum Hölder inequality applied to sequences of r-th powers of
sorted singular values.

With conjugate exponents `p' = p/r > 1` and `q' = q/r > 1` (which satisfy
`1/p' + 1/q' = 1` when `1/r = 1/p + 1/q`), this gives:
  `∑ σ↓ᵢ(A)^r · σ↓ᵢ(B)^r ≤ (∑ σ↓ᵢ(A)^p)^{r/p} · (∑ σ↓ᵢ(B)^q)^{r/q}`

Note: The sums on the RHS don't depend on the ordering, so we can replace
sorted singular values with unsorted ones.
entries.snippet:
lemma holder_step_for_singularValues (A B : Matrix d d ℂ)
    {r p q : ℝ} (hr : 0 < r) (hp : 0 < p) (hq : 0 < q)
    (hpqr : 1 / r = 1 / p + 1 / q) :
    (∑ i : Fin (Fintype.card d),
      (singularValuesSorted A i ^ r * singularValuesSorted B i ^ r)) ≤
    (∑ i : Fin (Fintype.card d), singularValuesSorted A i ^ p) ^ (r / p) *
    (∑ i : Fin (Fintype.card d), singularValuesSorted B i ^ q) ^ (r / q)

entries.name: Matrix.IsHermitian.eigenvalues_eq_of_unitary_similarity_diagonal
entries.docstring: If a Hermitian matrix A is unitarily similar to a diagonal matrix with real entries f, then the eigenvalues of A are a permutation of f.
entries.snippet:
lemma IsHermitian.eigenvalues_eq_of_unitary_similarity_diagonal {d 𝕜 : Type*}

entries.name: minimax
entries.docstring:
The minimax theorem, at the level of generality we need. For convex, compact, nonempty sets `S`
and `T`in a real topological vector space `M`, and a bilinear function `f` on M, we can exchange
the order of minimizing and maximizing.

  {M : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup M] [Module ℝ M] [ContinuousAdd M] [ContinuousSMul ℝ M] [FiniteDimensional ℝ M]

  (f : N →L[ℝ] M →L[ℝ] ℝ)
  (S : Set M) (T : Set N) (hS₁ : IsCompact S) (hT₁ : IsCompact T)
  (hS₂ : Convex ℝ S) (hT₂ : Convex ℝ T) (hS₃ : S.Nonempty) (hT₃ : T.Nonempty)
    : ⨅ x : T, ⨆ y : S, f x y = ⨆ y : S, ⨅ x : T, f x y

entries.name: MicroHamiltonian
entries.docstring:
The Hamiltonian for a microcanonical ensemble, parameterized by any extrinsic parameters of data D.
  Since it's an arbitrary type, 'T' would be nice, but we use 'D' for data to avoid confusion with temperature.
  We define Hamiltonians as an energy function on a real manifold, whose dimension n possibly depends on the data D.
  Energy is a WithTop ℝ, ⊤ is used to mean "excluded as a possibility in phase space".
  This formalization does exclude the possibility of discrete degrees of freedom; it is not _completely_ general.
  A better formalization could have an arbitrary measurable space.
entries.snippet:
structure MicroHamiltonian (D : Type) where
  dim : D → Type
  [dim_fin : ∀ d, Fintype (dim d)]
  H : {d : D} → (dim d → ℝ) → WithTop ℝ

entries.docstring: We add the dim_fin to the instance cache so that things like the measure can be synthesized
entries.snippet: instance microHamiltonianFintype (H : MicroHamiltonian D) (d : D) : Fintype (H.dim d)

entries.name: MicroHamiltonian.β_eq_deriv_S_U
entries.docstring:
The "definition of temperature from entropy":
1/T = (∂S/∂U), when the derivative is at constant extrinsic d (typically N/V).
Here we use β instead of 1/T on the left, and express the right actually as (∂S/∂β)/(∂U/∂β),
as all our things are ultimately parameterized by β.
entries.snippet: theorem β_eq_deriv_S_U {β : ℝ} (hi : H.ZIntegrable d β) : β = (deriv (H.EntropySβ d) β) / deriv (H.InternalU d) β
